newsitem.title: HONG KONG: H.K. stocks ease in early trade, utilities down.
newsitem.headline: H.K. stocks ease in early trade, utilities down.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks eased in early Tuesday trading chiefly due to selling pressure on utilities, brokers said.
""I think the market is affected by the poor peformance of utilities which led the market yesterday," said Patrick Chia, research director at China Everbright Research.
The Hang Seng Index slipped 32 points to 12,740, but off the morning's low of 12,731. Turnover was an active HK$1.35 billion.
The index was marked down chiefly on selling pressure on China Light and Hongkong Telecom, both of which performed well on Monday, brokers said.
China Light and Power fell HK$1.00 to HK$34.00 on the announcement that the government would ask the company to delay construction of its Black Point plant.

HongKong Telecom eased HK$0.15 to HK$13.55. The share put on HK$0.70 on Monday, chiefly on speculative buying fuelled by a London newspaper story that parent Cable and Wireless was seeking to sell a five percent stake in the Hong Kong company to a mainland Chinese company.
"I think for this week the market ...is just staying between 12,600 to 12,900. I think it had to take a break and then consolidate for awhile," said Chia.
Technical analysts said the index is likely to undergo further consolidation, although a rally on the heels of Wall Street's new high was not ruled out.

The Hang Seng Index and the Dow, which set a new closing high of 6,255.60 on Monday, could overshoot later in the week if the U.S. Federal Reserve left interest rates unchanged at its November 13 meeting, said Alex Wong, technical analyst at Dharmala Securities.
"I think upside is capped at 12,850 (for Tuesday), but we could see one-more rise to 13,000, likely later in the week, said Wong.
Daily indicators were already looking mixed, said Wong, adding that the move to 13,000 would be a good profit-taking opportunity.
The utilities sector led the market down, followed by properties. Finance counters held steady.
In the property sector, Great Eagle lost HK$0.35 to HK$28.90, while Amoy rose HK$0.15 to HK$9.95.
Banking giant HSBC Holdings was off HK$0.50 at HK$160.50 and Hang Seng Bank was up HK$0.25 at HK$94.25.
